clue.text: Story that may be recalled?

definitions.note: the defining word is also the whole wordplay: the two-word genre name reads identically back to front

indicators.note: recalled is taken as called back, read in reverse, and the letters come out unchanged that way round

parts.note: the defining word is also the whole wordplay: the two-word genre name reads identically back to front

explanation.surface: A tale that sticks in the memory, or one a publisher might withdraw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' says the entry reads the same backwards. An Aga saga is a British genre of novel about comfortable middle-class country life, named after the Aga range cooker in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: This genre label names a kind of popular novel, so it is a type of tale or narrative.

clue.text: Gunk, oily secretion and further marks on skin

parts.note: gunk is sticky muck, goo
sebum is the oily substance skin glands secrete
PS, a postscript, adds something further to a letter

explanation.surface: A list of unpleasant skin complaints: grime, grease and blemishes.
explanation.definitionFit: The bumps raised on skin by cold or fear are visible marks on it.

clue.text: Don't speak about a stocky cryptid's origin — man in gorilla suit probably?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the call for silence wraps the rest

parts.note: SH is the call for silence
squat means short and stocky

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Hush now about how this squat legendary beast began: probably just a man in a costume.
explanation.walkthrough: SH placed 'about' A + SQUAT + C. A cryptid is a creature, like Bigfoot, whose existence is unproven.
explanation.definitionFit: Sightings of the North American ape-man are often dismissed as a hoaxer wearing an ape costume.

clue.text: As some cars kept going, actual leaders blew up

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of the two words before it

parts.note: to blow up in anger is to rage, past tense raged

explanation.surface: Cars kept running while the real leaders lost their tempers.
explanation.definitionFit: Many cars are stored in a garage overnight, so they are kept that way.

clue.text: See 17
Observer of flies in house dropping wings to circle room

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes round the other piece
the wings of a word are its outer letters, here dropped

parts.note: taken as the word itself, to be trimmed
a cell is a small room

explanation.surface: Something watching flies in a house, losing its wings and circling a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping wings' leaves OUS from house; 'to circle' puts OUS around CELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Many insects, flies included, have simple eyes of this kind, so it is an organ of sight.

clue.text: Second, not the last, drink

indicators.note: the final letter is left off the synonym

parts.note: the latter is the second of two

explanation.surface: Ordering a second round, though not the final one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the last' removes the final R.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a milky coffee, a drink served in cafes.

clue.text: Market very much ahead of this country?

indicators.note: the first piece sits above the second in this down entry

parts.note: so means very much, as in 'so tired'
UK, the United Kingdom, from the British setter's viewpoint

explanation.surface: Is the market far in front in Britain?
explanation.definitionFit: It is an Arab marketplace or bazaar.

clue.text: Fresh brew now inside samovar

indicators.note: the mixed letters go within the vessel

parts.note: a samovar is a Russian tea urn

indicators.note: to brew is to mix up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fresh tea is brewing in the samovar right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brew' scrambles the word now, and 'inside' puts those letters within the tea vessel. The tea-making surface hides that Fresh means not yet worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing never worn is new, fresh from the shop.

clue.text: RC men not as desperate to see RC receptacle

indicators.note: desperate suggests wildness, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Roman Catholic men are not as keen as others to view a sacred vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the vessel in which the consecrated Host is displayed in Roman Catholic worship.

clue.text: Tense, as trained for audition?

indicators.note: audition here means hearing, so a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: trained means taught

explanation.surface: An actor trained for an audition and nervous about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for audition' signals a sound-alike: TAUGHT is heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense and stretched tight are synonyms, as of a rope or nerves.

clue.text: Nation combining games and sport

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school games
RU, rugby union

explanation.surface: A country that mixes play and athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a South American country, a nation.

clue.text: Tricky deliveries, balls containing opener for Gloucestershire

indicators.note: containing means the slang word holds the next piece

parts.note: goolies is British slang for testicles

indicators.note: an opener is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cricket report: devious bowling, with Gloucestershire's opening batsman facing the balls.
explanation.walkthrough: Gloucestershire is an English county cricket team, and an opener is a batsman as well as a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a googly is a deceptive ball from a leg-spinner that turns the unexpected way.

clue.text: Cold sweet provided, as cherry on top of dessert, some failing to eat it?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in the rest, as if eating it
failing suggests going wrong, so the letters of some are jumbled
on puts the colour above the next piece in this down entry

parts.note: if means provided that
cherry red is a colour, so red

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down entry is its first letter

explanation.surface: An iced pudding, served if a cherry sits on top, though some fail to eat it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' rearranges some into SEMO, and 'to eat' wraps it around the middle pieces; the dessert's top supplies D.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian semi-frozen dessert, so a chilled pudding or sweet course.

clue.text: However busy, I tend to get interrupted

parts.note: but means however

indicators.note: busy suggests bustle, so the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: A busy person complaining that they are always being cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: To butt in is to cut into a conversation, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Bank taken aback by the way one arranges locks

indicators.note: by puts the second piece beside the first

parts.note: ST, street, is a way

indicators.note: taken aback read literally means turned backwards

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on

explanation.surface: A riverbank surprised by a path, and somebody doing up a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdresser styles hair, and locks are tresses of hair.

clue.text: Opportunities are taken by those most alert, UKIP? Lousy organisation inspiring zero confidence, ultimately

definitions.text: Opportunities are taken by those most alert

parts.note: said as 'you kip', and to kip is to sleep or snooze

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the jumbled letters take in the next piece
organisation means arranging, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: zero is the letter O

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A jibe at the UK Independence Party as a shambolic outfit that wins no trust.
explanation.walkthrough: UKIP is a British right-wing party; its name read aloud is 'you kip'. 'organisation' turns LOUSY into YOULS, 'inspiring' takes in O, and E from confidence ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb warns that anyone slow to act misses chances, the same idea as the definition.

clue.text: Final issue finished, executed

parts.note: up means over, as in 'time's up'
shot as a method of execution

explanation.surface: The end of a matter: it was completed, carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: The outcome or end result of events is the final issue.

clue.text: Three bags found, every other piece nicked — it's a crime

indicators.note: nicked means stolen, so alternate letters are taken from the phrase

explanation.surface: Three bags of loot found, half the items stolen: an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 1st, 3rd, 5th letters and so on of THREEBAGSFOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country is a serious offence in law.

clue.text: Adorably cute, smart clothes chafe on end of nipple

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the stylish word dresses round the rest

parts.note: chic means smart, stylish

indicators.note: on places the rubbing after that letter
the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: to chafe is to rub

explanation.surface: A fashionable outfit rubbing at the nipple, though the look is sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb: the stylish word dresses round E, the nipple's final letter, followed by the chafing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a chubby-cheeked infant angel, so the adjective means sweetly innocent and cute.

clue.text: One visiting Cherbourg initially has to go across the Channel

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the town

parts.note: aller is the French verb for to go, French being spoken across the English Channel

explanation.surface: A traveller visiting the French port of Cherbourg must cross the Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor who calls at a house is someone paying a visit.

clue.text: English language once holding Germany back

indicators.note: the old tongue holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: Old Norse is a language no longer spoken
D, Germany's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: An old English language keeping Germany in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a reversal signal but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a proposal is to support or approve it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Cook retrospectively admitting problem with stock that's dropped down face, perhaps?

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the reversed name takes in the next piece

parts.note: Delia Smith is a famous British TV cook
BSE, mad cow disease, a problem with livestock

explanation.surface: A cook looking back admits a problem with soup stock that was spilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospectively' gives AILED from the cook's name. Stock means cattle here, not soup base, which is why the disease fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Descending a cliff or rock face by rope is the climbing technique named here; perhaps flags the example.

clue.text: Mental aberration naughty child masks in a good way

indicators.note: masks means covers, so the child word surrounds the next pieces

parts.note: a brat is a badly behaved child
far means a good distance

explanation.surface: A mental slip that a badly behaved child hides with good manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a momentary lapse of thought, so a mental slip.

clue.text: One right to fiddle with fiddler?

indicators.note: to fiddle with is to tamper, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R, right

explanation.surface: Someone entitled to play the violin alongside another violinist.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says the Roman emperor played music while Rome burned; the question mark marks this playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor is famed for having fiddled while his city burned, so he is a notable fiddler.

clue.text: See 23
Successor of Oscar Peterson arrives, and pianist ably starts

indicators.note: starts means the first letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: The heir of the jazz pianist Oscar Peterson arrives and plays skilfully.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar looks like part of the jazz name; it is the NATO phonetic alphabet's word for O.
explanation.definitionFit: In the radio spelling alphabet the code word for P follows the one for O.

clue.text: Depreciation in weapons, those used offensively

indicators.note: in places the loss of value within the weapons

parts.note: swords are weapons
wear, as in wear and tear, lowers value

explanation.surface: Weapons losing value through use, the kind wielded in attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used offensively' suggests weapons, but it means used to offend.
explanation.definitionFit: Profanities are terms people use to insult or shock, offensive language.

clue.text: Biblical punishment hurt, on being caught

indicators.note: the word on is caught inside the other piece

parts.note: to sting is to hurt

explanation.surface: A painful punishment from the Bible, inflicted when caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Execution by throwing rocks is a penalty described in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Grow old in retirement squeezing girl softly

indicators.note: the reversed word squeezes the girl's name inside it

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
P, piano, softly in music

explanation.surface: Getting older after retiring, and hugging a girl gently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' gives DLO. 'Grow old' looks like the definition, but only 'Grow' is; old belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To expand or mature, growing larger or more advanced, is a synonym.
